"""Compatibility detection: canonical invocation schema & validation rules.

Phase 1 / Area 1.A detection suite.  Every test fabricates an input, mutates
exactly one field, and asserts the real validator's rejection (or documents the
actual behavior when it differs from the plan).  No provider subprocess is
launched and no harness source module is modified.

The canonical baseline is copied verbatim from ``test_s2_contract._canonical``
so the two suites share the exact fixture shape.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

from orchestrator_harness.invocation import (
    CANONICAL_INVOCATION_SCHEMA,
    CanonicalInvocation,
    InvocationValidationError,
    _digest,
    _strings,
    adapt_coding_v1,
    adapt_invocation,
    parse_canonical_invocation,
)
import orchestrator_harness.lane_controller as controller
from orchestrator_harness.lane_controller import (
    InvocationError,
    _canonical_resume_admission_path,
    _canonical_resume_claims_accepted,
    _classify_provider_operations,
    _persist_canonical_acceptance,
    _provider_handoff_identity,
    _read_canonical_prior_status,
    _reject_ambiguous_coding_aliases,
    _validate_canonical_output_paths,
    isolated_coding_child_environment,
    load_invocation,
)
from orchestrator_harness.profile import RuntimeProfile
from orchestrator_harness.prompt_bundle import (
    PROMPT_BUNDLE_SCHEMA,
    prompt_bundle_record_from_paths,
)
from orchestrator_harness.provider import ProviderAdapterError
from orchestrator_harness.task import TASK_CARD_SCHEMA, record_sha256

CODING_INVOCATION_SCHEMA = "orchestrator-coding-invocation/v1"


class CompatInvocationRulesTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def _canonical(self, root: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, object], object]:
        """One valid ``orchestrator-worker-invocation/v1`` baseline (s2-identical)."""
        run = root / "run"
        workspace = run / ".agent-workspace"
        workspace.mkdir(parents=True)
        runtime = root / "runtime"
        runtime.mkdir()
        prompt_a = run / "prompt-a.md"
        prompt_b = run / "prompt-b.md"
        prompt_a.write_bytes(b"workflow\n")
        prompt_b.write_bytes(b"task\n")
        card = {
            "schema": TASK_CARD_SCHEMA,
            "card_id": "card-1",
            "lane_id": "lane-1",
            "stage_cohort_id": "cohort-1",
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "objective": "Do the bounded task",
            "revision": "r1",
        }
        profile = RuntimeProfile(
            "profile-1",
            "implementer",
            "claude-code",
            "claude-test",
            ("Read",),
            ("repo",),
            ("resource-1",),
            ("CLAUDE_CODE_TEST",),
            ("WORKFLOW_TEST_FLAG",),
        )
        bundle = prompt_bundle_record_from_paths(
            workflow_id="workflow-1",
            task_card_id="card-1",
            profile_id="profile-1",
            paths=(("instructions", prompt_a), ("task", prompt_b)),
            run_root=run,
        )
        value: dict[str, object] = {
            "schema": CANONICAL_INVOCATION_SCHEMA,
            "action": "start",
            "run_root": str(run),
            "runtime_root": str(runtime),
            "lane_id": "lane-1",
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "cohort_id": "cohort-1",
            "workflow": {"id": "workflow-1", "version": "1"},
            "task_card": {
                "id": "card-1",
                "revision": "r1",
                "sha256": record_sha256(card),
            },
            "role": "implementer",
            "provider": {
                "id": "claude-code",
                "model": "claude-test",
                "command": ["synthetic-claude"],
                "permission_mode": "default",
                "allowed_tools": ["Read"],
            },
            "profile": profile.to_record(),
            "prompt_bundle": bundle,
            "output_paths": {
                "status": str(workspace / "worker_controller.status.json"),
                "jsonl": str(workspace / "worker_provider.jsonl"),
                "stderr": str(workspace / "worker.stderr.log"),
                "last_message": str(workspace / "worker.last-message"),
            },
            "event_log_path": str(runtime / "events.jsonl"),
            "resources": ["resource-1"],
        }
        return value, card

    def _coding_v1_record(self) -> dict[str, object]:
        """One valid ``orchestrator-coding-invocation/v1`` baseline (s2-identical)."""
        return {
            "schema": CODING_INVOCATION_SCHEMA,
            "action": "start",
            "run_root": "C:/run",
            "runtime_root": "C:/runtime",
            "prompt_path": "C:/run/prompt.md",
            "prompt_sha256": "a" * 64,
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "lane_id": "lane-1",
            "task": "coding-task",
            "phase": "implementation",
            "event_log_path": "C:/runtime/events.jsonl",
            "output_paths": {
                "status": "C:/run/.agent-workspace/status.json",
                "jsonl": "C:/run/.agent-workspace/provider.jsonl",
                "stderr": "C:/run/.agent-workspace/stderr.log",
                "last_message": "C:/run/.agent-workspace/last-message",
            },
            "codex": {
                "model": "codex-test",
                "reasoning_effort": "medium",
                "service_tier": "priority",
                "sandbox": "workspace-write",
                "approval_policy": "never",
            },
        }

    # C2 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c2_action_must_be_start_or_resume(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            bad = dict(raw)
            bad["action"] = "foo"
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(InvocationValidationError, "action"):
                parse_canonical_invocation(bad)
            start = parse_canonical_invocation(raw)
            self.assertEqual("start", start.action)
            resume = dict(raw)
            resume["action"] = "resume"
            resume["resume"] = {"session_id": "session-1"}
            parsed_resume = parse_canonical_invocation(resume)
            self.assertEqual("resume", parsed_resume.action)
            self.assertEqual("session-1", parsed_resume.requested_session_id)

    # C3 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c3_resume_requires_non_empty_session_id(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            missing = dict(raw)
            missing["action"] = "resume"
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationValidationError):
                parse_canonical_invocation(missing)
            empty = dict(raw)
            empty["action"] = "resume"
            empty["resume"] = {"session_id": ""}
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "session_id"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(empty)

    # C4 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c4_start_cannot_carry_resume_block(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            raw["resume"] = {"session_id": "session-1"}
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "cannot contain resume"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    # C5 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c5_provider_notification_must_be_boolean(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            bad = dict(raw)
            bad["provider"] = {
                **raw["provider"],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                "notification": "yes",
            }
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "notification"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(bad)
            for value in (True, False):
                ok = dict(raw)
                ok["provider"] = {
                    **raw["provider"],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                    "notification": value,
                }
                parsed = parse_canonical_invocation(ok)
                self.assertIn("notification", parsed.provider_options)

    # C6 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c6_profile_role_must_match_invocation_role(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            profile = dict(raw["profile"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            profile["role"] = "reviewer"
            raw["profile"] = profile
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "profile.role"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    # C7 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c7_profile_provider_must_match_provider_id(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            profile = dict(raw["profile"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            profile["provider"] = "codex"
            raw["profile"] = profile
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "profile.provider"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    # C8 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c8_profile_model_must_match_provider_model(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            profile = dict(raw["profile"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            profile["model"] = "different-model"
            raw["profile"] = profile
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "profile.model"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    # C9 ---------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c9_prompt_bundle_schema_and_version_validation(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            self.assertEqual(PROMPT_BUNDLE_SCHEMA, raw["prompt_bundle"]["schema"])  # type: ignore[index]
            wrong_schema = dict(raw)
            bundle = dict(raw["prompt_bundle"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            bundle["schema"] = "bogus-bundle/v1"
            wrong_schema["prompt_bundle"] = bundle
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "schema/version"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(wrong_schema)
            wrong_version = dict(raw)
            bundle = dict(raw["prompt_bundle"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            bundle["version"] = 2
            wrong_version["prompt_bundle"] = bundle
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "schema/version"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(wrong_version)

    # C10 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c10_resume_identity_must_be_an_object(self) -> None:
        # Coding-v1 exposes the field literally named "resume_identity".
        bad = self._coding_v1_record()
        bad["resume_identity"] = "not-an-object"
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            InvocationValidationError, "resume_identity"
        ):
            adapt_coding_v1(bad)
        ok = self._coding_v1_record()
        ok["resume_identity"] = {
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "thread_id": "thread-1",
        }
        adapted = adapt_coding_v1(ok)
        self.assertEqual("thread-1", adapted.requested_session_id)
        # The canonical route shares the object guard via the resume block.
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            raw["action"] = "resume"
            raw["resume"] = "not-an-object"
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "resume.*object"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(raw)

    # C11 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c11_unknown_invocation_schema_rejected(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            InvocationValidationError, "unsupported invocation schema"
        ):
            adapt_invocation({"schema": "bogus/v1"})
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            path = root / "bogus.invocation.json"
            path.write_text(json.dumps({"schema": "bogus/v1"}), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationError, "unsupported invocation schema"
            ):
                load_invocation(path)

    # C16 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c16_ambiguous_coding_aliases_rejected(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(InvocationError, "ambiguous"):
            _reject_ambiguous_coding_aliases(
                {"codex": {}, "codex_settings": {}}
            )
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(InvocationError, "ambiguous"):
            _reject_ambiguous_coding_aliases(
                {"resume_identity": {}, "resume": {}}
            )
        _reject_ambiguous_coding_aliases({"codex": {}})
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            coding = self._coding_v1_record()
            coding["codex_settings"] = dict(coding["codex"])  # type: ignore[index]
            path = root / "ambiguous.invocation.json"
            path.write_text(json.dumps(coding), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(InvocationError, "ambiguous"):
                load_invocation(path)

    # C18 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c18_canonical_output_path_safety_and_uniqueness(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            start_path = root / "start.invocation.json"
            start_path.write_text(json.dumps(raw), encoding="utf-8")
            invocation = load_invocation(start_path)
            outputs = {
                "status": invocation.status_path,
                "jsonl": invocation.jsonl_path,
                "stderr": invocation.stderr_path,
                "last_message": invocation.last_message_path,
            }
            # Unique safe paths are accepted.
            _validate_canonical_output_paths(
                outputs, workspace=invocation.workspace
            )
            # Duplicate output paths are rejected.
            duplicated = dict(outputs)
            duplicated["jsonl"] = duplicated["status"]
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "pairwise distinct"
            ):
                _validate_canonical_output_paths(
                    duplicated, workspace=invocation.workspace
                )
            # A ``../`` traversal output path is rejected at load time: the
            # traversal guard lives in ``_safe_path``/``_load_canonical_invocation``
            # rather than in ``_validate_canonical_output_paths`` (which handles
            # pairwise uniqueness and reserved-artifact collisions only).
            traversal = json.loads(json.dumps(raw))
            output_paths = dict(traversal["output_paths"])  # type: ignore[arg-type]
            output_paths["jsonl"] = str(
                root / "run" / ".agent-workspace" / ".." / "outside.json"
            )
            traversal["output_paths"] = output_paths
            traversal_path = root / "traversal.invocation.json"
            traversal_path.write_text(json.dumps(traversal), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(InvocationError, "escapes"):
                load_invocation(traversal_path)

    # C19 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c19_sha256_hex_digest_format(self) -> None:
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            InvocationValidationError, "SHA-256 hex digest"
        ):
            _digest("a" * 63, "task_card.sha256")
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            InvocationValidationError, "SHA-256 hex digest"
        ):
            _digest("g" * 64, "task_card.sha256")
        self.assertEqual("a" * 64, _digest("A" * 64, "task_card.sha256"))
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            short = dict(raw)
            short["task_card"] = {
                **short["task_card"],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                "sha256": "a" * 63,
            }
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationValidationError):
                parse_canonical_invocation(short)
            nonhex = dict(raw)
            nonhex["task_card"] = {
                **nonhex["task_card"],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                "sha256": "g" * 64,
            }
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationValidationError):
                parse_canonical_invocation(nonhex)
            uppercase = dict(raw)
            uppercase["task_card"] = {
                **uppercase["task_card"],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                "sha256": "A" * 64,
            }
            self.assertEqual(
                "a" * 64,
                parse_canonical_invocation(uppercase).task_card_sha256,
            )
            parsed = parse_canonical_invocation(raw)
            self.assertEqual(64, len(parsed.task_card_sha256))

    # C20 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c20_string_list_no_duplicates(self) -> None:
        # The plan names ``_string_list``; the no-duplicates guard actually
        # lives in ``invocation._strings``.  ``lane_controller._string_list``
        # intentionally allows duplicates (it is a shape-only helper), so the
        # canonical route rejects duplicates through the parser, which runs
        # first inside ``_load_canonical_invocation``.
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            InvocationValidationError, "duplicates"
        ):
            _strings(["Read", "Read"], "provider.allowed_tools")
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            dup = dict(raw)
            dup["provider"] = {
                **raw["provider"],  # type: ignore[arg-type]
                "allowed_tools": ["Read", "Read"],
            }
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationValidationError, "duplicates"
            ):
                parse_canonical_invocation(dup)
            path = root / "dup-tools.invocation.json"
            path.write_text(json.dumps(dup), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationError):
                load_invocation(path)

    # C21 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c21_isolated_coding_child_environment_strips_secrets(self) -> None:
        env, cleared = isolated_coding_child_environment(
            {
                "PATH": "C:/bin",
                "PYTHONUTF8": "1",
                "MCP_ENDPOINT": "ambient",
                "CREDENTIAL_ATLAS_TOKEN": "secret",
                "SECRET_API_KEY": "secret",
                "TOKEN_GITHUB": "secret",
                "TARGET_BOARD": "hardware",
                "ANTHROPIC_API_KEY": "credential",
                "GITHUB_TOKEN": "credential",
            }
        )
        self.assertEqual({"PATH": "C:/bin", "PYTHONUTF8": "1"}, env)
        self.assertEqual(
            [
                "CREDENTIAL_ATLAS_TOKEN",
                "MCP_ENDPOINT",
                "SECRET_API_KEY",
                "TARGET_BOARD",
                "TOKEN_GITHUB",
            ],
            cleared,
        )
        self.assertNotIn("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY", env)
        self.assertNotIn("GITHUB_TOKEN", env)

    # C22 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c22_prior_canonical_acceptance_read_and_persist_byte_stable(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            start_path = root / "start.invocation.json"
            start_path.write_text(json.dumps(raw), encoding="utf-8")
            invocation = load_invocation(start_path)
            status_path = invocation.status_path
            prior = {
                "schema": "orchestrator-lane-controller/v1",
                "state": "PROVIDER_EXITED",
                "invocation_schema": CANONICAL_INVOCATION_SCHEMA,
                "worker_invocation_id": raw["worker_invocation_id"],
                "provider_id": "claude-code",
                "resume_identity": {
                    "task_card_id": "card-1",
                    "terminal_acceptance_state": "PENDING",
                },
            }
            status_path.write_text(json.dumps(prior), encoding="utf-8")
            found = _read_canonical_prior_status(invocation)
            self.assertIsNotNone(found)
            path, value = found
            self.assertEqual(status_path, path)
            self.assertEqual("PROVIDER_EXITED", value["state"])

            acceptance_identity = {
                "accepted_commit": "a" * 40,
                "accepted_by": "ROOT-IM",
            }
            updated = _persist_canonical_acceptance(
                status_path, value, acceptance_identity
            )
            self.assertEqual("ACCEPTED", updated["terminal_acceptance_state"])
            self.assertEqual("ACCEPTED", updated["task_advancement_state"])
            self.assertEqual(
                "ACCEPTED",
                updated["resume_identity"]["terminal_acceptance_state"],
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                "ACCEPTED", updated["resume_identity"]["task_advancement_state"]
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                acceptance_identity,
                updated["resume_identity"]["acceptance_identity"],
            )
            self.assertEqual(updated, json.loads(status_path.read_text()))
            first_bytes = status_path.read_bytes()
            # Byte-stable: persisting the already-updated status again yields
            # identical bytes (deterministic sort_keys/indent serialization).
            again = _persist_canonical_acceptance(
                status_path, updated, acceptance_identity
            )
            self.assertEqual(updated, again)
            self.assertEqual(first_bytes, status_path.read_bytes())

    # C23 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_c23_canonical_resume_admission_path_and_claims(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)
            start_path = root / "start.invocation.json"
            start_path.write_text(json.dumps(raw), encoding="utf-8")
            invocation = load_invocation(start_path)
            assert invocation.canonical is not None
            workspace = invocation.workspace
            self.assertEqual(
                workspace / "RESUME_ADMISSION.json",
                _canonical_resume_admission_path(invocation),
            )
            custom = replace(
                invocation,
                canonical=replace(
                    invocation.canonical,
                    resume_admission_path=Path("custom/RESUME_ADMISSION.json"),
                ),
            )
            self.assertEqual(
                workspace / "custom" / "RESUME_ADMISSION.json",
                _canonical_resume_admission_path(custom),
            )
            escaping = replace(
                invocation,
                canonical=replace(
                    invocation.canonical,
                    resume_admission_path=Path("..") / "escape.json",
                ),
            )
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(InvocationError, "escapes"):
                _canonical_resume_admission_path(escaping)

            # Valid claims accepted: top-level or nested resume_identity.
            top_level = {
                "schema": "orchestrator-lane-controller/v1",
                "terminal_acceptance_state": "ACCEPTED",
            }
            self.assertTrue(
                _canonical_resume_claims_accepted(invocation, top_level)
            )
            nested = {
                "schema": "orchestrator-lane-controller/v1",
                "resume_identity": {"task_advancement_state": "ACCEPTED"},
            }
            self.assertTrue(
                _canonical_resume_claims_accepted(invocation, nested)
            )
            # Tampered claims rejected: no ACCEPTED anywhere and no valid
            # RESULT.json exists in the workspace.
            tampered = {
                "schema": "orchestrator-lane-controller/v1",
                "terminal_acceptance_state": "PENDING",
                "resume_identity": {"terminal_acceptance_state": "PENDING"},
            }
            self.assertFalse(
                _canonical_resume_claims_accepted(invocation, tampered)
            )

    def test_c24_provider_operation_classification_and_handoff_identity(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        launch = _classify_provider_operations("claude-code", ["launch"])
        self.assertEqual("launch", launch[0]["operation"])
        self.assertTrue(launch[0]["supported"])
        resume_ops = _classify_provider_operations(
            "claude-code", ["launch", "resume"]
        )
        resume = next(record for record in resume_ops if record["operation"] == "resume")
        self.assertTrue(resume["supported"])
        # FINDING (C24, lane_controller.py:1692-1699): an operation outside
        # PROVIDER_OPERATION_NAMES does NOT yield the intended unsupported
        # record -- _classify_provider_operations routes it straight into
        # unsupported_operation_result, which itself raises
        # ProviderAdapterError("unknown provider operation").  The
        # unsupported-record branch is therefore unreachable; the actual,
        # documented behavior is a raise.  No mutation is silently accepted.
        with self.assertRaises(ProviderAdapterError):
            _classify_provider_operations("claude-code", ["teleport"])

            role, logical_task_id = _provider_handoff_identity(invocation)

            self.assertEqual(

                _provider_handoff_identity(invocation),
            )

    # C13 / C14 / C1 guards --------------------------------------------------

    def test_c13_c14_c1_closed_shape_and_repository_guards(self) -> None:
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as temporary:
            root = Path(temporary)
            raw, _ = self._canonical(root)

            # C1: canonical top-level closed shape.
            unknown_field = dict(raw)
            unknown_field["unknown_field"] = True
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationValidationError):
                parse_canonical_invocation(unknown_field)
            missing_required = dict(raw)
            del missing_required["role"]
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationValidationError):
                parse_canonical_invocation(missing_required)

            # C13: repository closed shape (parse level, no git needed).
            repository = {
                "common_dir": str(root / "git-common"),
                "worktree_root": str(root / "run"),
                "branch": "coding",
                "base_commit": "0" * 40,
            }
            with_repo = dict(raw)
            with_repo["repository"] = repository
            parsed = parse_canonical_invocation(with_repo)
            assert parsed.repository is not None
            self.assertEqual("0" * 40, parsed.repository["base_commit"])
            bad_repo = dict(raw)
            bad_repo["repository"] = {**repository, "origin": "https://x.invalid"}
            with self.assertRaises(InvocationValidationError):
                parse_canonical_invocation(bad_repo)

            # C14: repository.worktree_root must equal run_root (load level).
            (root / "git-common").mkdir()
            (root / "elsewhere").mkdir()
            mismatched = dict(raw)
            mismatched["repository"] = {
                **repository,
                "worktree_root": str(root / "elsewhere"),
            }
            mismatched_path = root / "mismatched-repo.invocation.json"
            mismatched_path.write_text(json.dumps(mismatched), encoding="utf-8")
            with self.assertRaisesRegex(
                InvocationError, "worktree_root must equal run_root"
            ):
                load_invocation(mismatched_path)

"""Compatibility detection: resume & handoff admission gates (Phase 1 / 1.G).

Detection-only suite over fabricated identity / amendment / invocation /
preflight-bundle inputs.  No provider subprocess is launched and no harness
source module is modified.  Where the real validator differs from the plan's
description, the ACTUAL behavior is pinned by a green assertion and the
divergence is recorded as a FINDING next to the test that pins it (see K8).
"""

import hashlib
import json
import tempfile
import unittest
from collections.abc import Mapping
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

)
from orchestrator_harness.invocation import (

from orchestrator_harness.prompt_bundle import prompt_bundle_record_from_paths

    RESUME_AMENDMENT_REVIEW_SCHEMA,

    validate_resume_amendment_review,
)
from orchestrator_harness.task import TASK_CARD_SCHEMA, record_sha256
from orchestrator_harness.tests.support import TemporaryGitRepository, write_json

CODING_INVOCATION_SCHEMA = "orchestrator-coding-invocation/v1"


class CompatResumeAdmissionTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """K2-K8: the resume identity gate and the amendment review record."""

    def _canonical(self, root: Path) -> tuple[dict[str, object], dict[str, object]]:

        prompt_a.write_bytes(b"workflow\n")

        card = {

    @staticmethod
    def _write_canonical_json(path: Path, value: dict[str, object]) -> str:
        data = json.dumps(
            value, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False
        ).encode("utf-8")
        path.write_bytes(data)
        return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()

    def _resume_identity(
        self,
        canonical: CanonicalInvocation,
        *,
        session_id: str = "session-1",
        starting_commit: str = "a" * 40,
        **overrides: object,
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """A requested/persisted resume identity bound to a live identity."""
        value = canonical.identity(session_id=session_id, starting_commit=starting_commit)
        value["live_identity"] = {
            "provider_id": canonical.provider_id,
            "session_id": session_id,
        }
        value.update(overrides)
        return value

    def _same_job_identity(
        self, raw: Mapping[str, object], root: Path, *, session_id: str = "session-1"
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """The 12-key closed same-job identity the s2 review carries."""
        return {
            "card_id": raw["task_card"]["id"],  # type: ignore[index]
            "stage_cohort_id": raw["cohort_id"],
            "worker_invocation_id": raw["worker_invocation_id"],

            "original_base_commit": "0" * 40,
            "continuation_start_commit": "0" * 40,
            "exclusive_resources": list(raw["resources"]),  # type: ignore[arg-type]
        }

    def _amendment_review(
        self,
        *,
        requested: Mapping[str, object],
        persisted: Mapping[str, object],
        same_job_identity: Mapping[str, object],
        old_card: Path,
        new_card: Path,
        old_prompt: Path,
        new_prompt: Path,
        disposition: str = "NO_CONTINUATION_REQUIRED",
        classification: str = "HARMLESS",
    ) -> dict[str, object]:
        """One strict ROOT-owned amendment review over two reviewed pairs."""

        def pair(old_path: Path, new_path: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
            return {
                "old_path": str(old_path),
                "old_sha256": hashlib.sha256(old_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                "new_path": str(new_path),
                "new_sha256": hashlib.sha256(new_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest(),
                "diff": {
                    "command": f"git diff --no-index -- {old_path} {new_path}",
                    "working_directory": str(old_path.parent),
                    "exit_code": 1,
                    "stdout_encoding": "utf-8",
                    "stdout_sha256": "a" * 64,
                    "stdout_bytes": 1,
                    "stderr_sha256": "b" * 64,
                    "stderr_bytes": 0,
                },
            }

        return {
            "schema": RESUME_AMENDMENT_REVIEW_SCHEMA,
            "run_id": "synthetic-run",
            "stage_id": "S2",
            "lane_id": requested["lane_id"],
            "recorded_utc": "2026-01-01T00:00:00Z",
            "recorded_by": "ROOT-IM",
            "disposition": disposition,
            "job_state": "UNACCEPTED",
            "same_job_identity": dict(same_job_identity),
            "reviewed_pairs": {
                "task_card": pair(old_card, new_card),
                "prompt": pair(old_prompt, new_prompt),
            },
            "semantic_impact": {
                "classification": classification,
                "rationale": "ROOT reviewed this exact pair for the resume admission test.",
                "affected_scope": ["canonical resume identity"],
                "preserved_credit": ["unaffected prior checks"],

            "route": {

                "rerun_only_affected_checks": True,
                "require_fresh_affected_review": False,

            predicate = cast(Mapping[str, object], item).get("predicate")

        artifacts: set[str] = set()
        for item in cast(list[object], failures):

            record = cast(Mapping[str, object], item)

    def test_k8_thread_id_precedence_is_conflict_rejection(self) -> None:
        base = self._coding_v1_record()
        # (a) Both fields present and equal → accepted; the resolved thread is
        # that shared value.
        equal = dict(base)
        equal["resume_thread_id"] = "thread-1"
        equal["resume_identity"] = {
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "thread_id": "thread-1",
        }
        adapted = adapt_coding_v1(equal)
        self.assertEqual("thread-1", adapted.requested_session_id)

        # Legacy-only and canonical-only spellings each resolve to their value.
        legacy_only = dict(base)
        legacy_only["resume_thread_id"] = "thread-legacy"
        self.assertEqual(
            "thread-legacy", adapt_coding_v1(legacy_only).requested_session_id
        )
        canonical_only = dict(base)
        canonical_only["resume_identity"] = {
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "thread_id": "thread-canonical",
        }
        self.assertEqual(
            "thread-canonical", adapt_coding_v1(canonical_only).requested_session_id
        )

        # (b) FINDING (K8, invocation.py:716-722): the plan describes "canonical
        # wins per documented precedence" (phase-1 §1.G K8), but the real
        # coding-v1 adapter does NOT let resume_identity.thread_id silently win.
        # When both fields are present and differ it fails closed by raising, so
        # a conflicting legacy value can never be dropped without detection.
        conflicting = dict(base)
        conflicting["resume_thread_id"] = "thread-legacy"
        conflicting["resume_identity"] = {
            "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
            "thread_id": "thread-canonical",
        }
        with self.assertRaisesRegex(
            InvocationValidationError, "conflicting requested resume thread IDs"
        ):
            adapt_coding_v1(conflicting)

                        "exit_code": 1,
                        "stdout_encoding": "utf-8",
                        "stdout_sha256": "a" * 64,
                        "stdout_bytes": 0,
                        "stderr_sha256": "b" * 64,
                        "stderr_bytes": 0,
                    },
                }
                for name, path, digest in (
                    ("task_card", self.task_card_path, task_hash),
                    ("prompt", self.prompt_path, prompt_hash),
                )
            },
            "semantic_impact": {
                "classification": "HARMLESS",
                "rationale": "The exact reviewed pair has no semantic change.",
                "affected_scope": ["none"],
                "preserved_credit": ["all prior checks"],
            },
            "route": {
                "kind": "EXACT_REVIEWED_PAIR",
                "resume_same_worker": True,
                "resume_same_provider_session": True,
                "reopen_accepted_tasks": False,
                "rerun_only_affected_checks": True,
                "require_fresh_affected_review": False,
            },
        }
        write_json(review_path, review)
        return review

    def preflight(self, *required: Path) -> dict[str, object]:
        return preflight_handoff(
            task_card_path=self.task_card_path,
            invocation_path=self.invocation_path,
            result_path=self.result_path,
            dependency_map_path=self.dependency_map_path,
            worktree=self.worktree,
            evidence_root=self.workspace,
            required_evidence=required or (Path("proof.json"),),
        )

    @staticmethod
    def _failed_predicates(result: Mapping[str, object]) -> set[str]:
        failures = result.get("failed_predicates")
        if not isinstance(failures, list):
            raise TypeError("preflight failed_predicates must be a list")
        predicates: set[str] = set()
        for item in cast(list[object], failures):
            if not isinstance(item, Mapping):
                raise TypeError("preflight failure must be an object")
            predicate = cast(Mapping[str, object], item).get("predicate")
            if not isinstance(predicate, str):
                raise TypeError("preflight failure predicate must be a string")
            predicates.add(predicate)
        return predicates

    @staticmethod
    def _artifacts_for(result: Mapping[str, object], predicate: str) -> set[str]:
        failures = result.get("failed_predicates")
        if not isinstance(failures, list):
            raise TypeError("preflight failed_predicates must be a list")
        artifacts: set[str] = set()
        for item in cast(list[object], failures):
            if not isinstance(item, Mapping):
                continue
            record = cast(Mapping[str, object], item)
            if record.get("predicate") == predicate:
                artifact = record.get("artifact")
                if isinstance(artifact, str):
                    artifacts.add(artifact)
        return artifacts

    # K10 --------------------------------------------------------------------

    def test_k10_complete_bundle_passes(self) -> None:
        result = self.preflight()
        self.assertEqual(PASS, result["disposition"])
        self.assertEqual([], result["failed_predicates"])

    def test_k10_missing_invocation_file_blocks_with_distinct_reason(self) -> None:
        self.invocation_path.unlink()
        result = self.preflight()
        self.assertEqual(REPORT_ONLY_ERROR, result["disposition"])
        self.assertIn("JSON_OBJECT", self._failed_predicates(result))
        self.assertEqual({"invocation"}, self._artifacts_for(result, "JSON_OBJECT"))

    def test_k10_amendment_identity_mismatch_blocks_with_distinct_reason(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        review = self._amendment_review_record()
        review_path = self.root / "RESUME_ADMISSION.json"
        review_hash = hashlib.sha256(review_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        task_hash = hashlib.sha256(self.task_card_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        prompt_hash = hashlib.sha256(self.prompt_path.read_bytes()).hexdigest()
        dependency_map = cast(
            dict[str, object],
            json.loads(self.dependency_map_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")),
        )
        dependency_map["amendment"] = {
            "review_path": str(review_path),
            "review_sha256": review_hash,
            "disposition": "NO_CONTINUATION_REQUIRED",
            "requested_identity": {
                "task_card_id": "card-1",
                "lane_id": "S3.P",
                "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
                "task_card_sha256": task_hash,
                "prompt_content_sha256": prompt_hash,
            },
            "persisted_identity": {
                "task_card_id": "card-1",
                "lane_id": "S3.P",
                "worker_invocation_id": "worker-1",
                "task_card_sha256": task_hash,
                "prompt_content_sha256": prompt_hash,
            },
            "job_identity": cast(dict[str, object], review["same_job_identity"]),
        }
        write_json(self.dependency_map_path, dependency_map)
        bound = self.preflight()
        self.assertEqual(PASS, bound["disposition"])

        # Corrupt the declared review hash: the amendment identity is now the
        # single distinct blocker.
        dependency_map["amendment"]["review_sha256"] = "0" * 64  # type: ignore[index]
        write_json(self.dependency_map_path, dependency_map)
        mismatched = self.preflight()
        self.assertEqual(REPORT_ONLY_ERROR, mismatched["disposition"])
        self.assertIn(
            "RESUME_AMENDMENT_IDENTITY", self._failed_predicates(mismatched)
        )
        self.assertEqual(
            {"amendment"},
            self._artifacts_for(mismatched, "RESUME_AMENDMENT_IDENTITY"),
        )

    def test_k10_missing_required_evidence_blocks_with_distinct_reason(
        self,
    ) -> None:
        result = self.preflight(Path("missing-proof.json"))
        self.assertEqual(INCOMPLETE, result["disposition"])
        self.assertIn("REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_EXISTS", self._failed_predicates(result))
        self.assertEqual(
            {"required_evidence"},
            self._artifacts_for(result, "REQUIRED_EVIDENCE_EXISTS"),
        )


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
